Common Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

Q

How much does a K-12 access control system cost?

Costs vary widely based on facility size, number of doors, and platform choice. A single-school deployment typically ranges from $30,000 to $150,000. Multi-campus district deployments can run $500,000+. We provide free assessments that include detailed budget projections.

Q

What is the difference between access control and a door lock?

A door lock is mechanical — it requires a physical key and provides no audit trail. An access control system uses electronic credentials (cards, fobs, mobile), records every entry/exit event, can be managed remotely, and supports time-based scheduling and instant lockdown capability.

Q

How long does installation take?

A single-school project typically takes 2–6 weeks depending on the number of doors and wiring complexity. We plan all installations to minimize disruption to the school day — weekend and after-hours work is standard.

Q

Can we integrate with our existing cameras?

Yes — most modern access control platforms support video integration. We assess your existing camera system and either integrate it or recommend an upgrade path that aligns with your access control investment.

Q

What happens to access during a power outage?

Properly designed systems include battery backup at the door controller level. Doors can be configured to fail-safe (unlock) or fail-secure (stay locked) based on life-safety requirements for each location.

Q

Do you offer ongoing support after installation?

Yes. We offer annual support contracts that include software updates, troubleshooting, and on-site service. Many of our clients have worked with us for 5+ years across multiple upgrade cycles.
